s: Hello everyone, and welcome to Muse English!
Today we are talking about money and shopping.
Shopping is something we do every day.
We buy food, we buy clothes, and we pay for many things.
Today we will learn five useful words: coin, pay, bill, card, and expensive.
A coin is a small round piece of metal money.
It is money, but it is not paper money.
In many countries, small things cost only a coin.
For example, you can buy a candy for one coin.
I always have a few coins in my pocket.
Yesterday I found a coin on the street.
But one coin is not enough for big things.
A coin is only good for small things.
When you want to buy something, you must pay.
To pay means to give money for something you buy.
When you pay for your lunch, you give money to the restaurant.
When you pay for a bus ticket, you give money to the driver.
Every day we pay for many things.
I pay for my coffee in the morning.
I pay for my groceries in the evening.
Sometimes we pay with a card.
The bill is the paper that shows how much money you must pay.
In a restaurant, after you eat, the waiter brings the bill to your table.
The bill shows the price of your food.
You read the bill, you see the total, and then you pay.
One time the bill was wrong.
I was happy that I read the bill.
Always read the bill before you pay.

A card is a small plastic thing.
You use it to pay instead of money.
You do not need cash when you have a card.
You just give the card, and the money comes from your bank.
I use my card every day.
I pay for my lunch with my card.
I pay for the bus with my card.
But be careful with your card.
And never tell other people your card number.
Something is expensive when it costs a lot of money.
A small candy is not expensive.
But a new car is expensive.
A big house is very expensive.
Yesterday I saw a beautiful watch.
I wanted to buy it, but it was too expensive for me.
The watch was expensive, so I did not buy it.
When something is expensive, we must think.
Last week I went shopping with my friend Sara.
We had lunch in a small restaurant.
Did you pay for the lunch?
First, the waiter brought the bill.
The bill was not too big.
Then Sara wanted to pay with her card, but she forgot her card at home.
After lunch, we walked to a shop.
It was a beautiful bag, but it was expensive.
I will not pay that much for a bag." So we left the shop.
On the way home, I found a coin on the sidewalk.
I gave the coin to Sara.
I said, "This coin is for your next small shopping."
